brief: Gold rebounded after the Fed hike despite the 10-year yield moving above 5% and a stronger dollar, but by 24 September it had given that rebound back as yields and DXY climbed further, testing whether it can withstand the rate pressure. GS frames two buyer types: patient official-sector buyers and faster ETF investors. Central bank gold buying is running at a seasonally adjusted 91 tonnes a month over the past three months, versus 17 tonnes before 2022, with GS forecasting 60 tonnes a month through 2027 as support. ETF flows are more volatile: global gold ETFs shed 74 tonnes in June, added 23 in July and 121 in August per the World Gold Council, so funds were buying heavily just before the September rate shock. GS cut its end-2026 target to $4,650 from $4,900, kept its end-2027 target at $5,400, and flagged call option positioning near three times its historical average. In a more hawkish Fed scenario (not GS's base case), gold falls toward $4,070 before a partial recovery to $4,200 by year-end. Thesis: central banks may not absorb every ETF sale or options unwind, so fast money can leave before patient buyers show up. Watch whether gold holds again against rates and the dollar.
